raw_response:
I farm the way I always do: I start from what worked last year, then I change a little if I think the return is worth the money. I have only 8 mu, so every bag of fertilizer counts, but I still would rather put a bit more than come up short and lose yield. In Quzhou our wheat and maize can do well with well water, so I will keep most of my land in the wheat-maize rotation and leave a smaller piece for cotton. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize because I have seen people around me get steadier yield with them. For cotton, I will not push the area too big because it takes more watching and more sprays. On wheat I will feed it heavier because that crop shows quickly if fertilizer is short; maize I will also feed enough because it follows wheat and I want the stubble land to keep producing. Cotton needs less land from me, but I will still give it enough potash and more pest watching. I do not like fancy changes. I will do solid field prep, enough fertilizer, count my irrigations carefully, and aim for a stable harvest from all three crops.
